corrections.source_says: Set to met under the supplied codebook: judges scored the quality of participant-produced architectural designs. The codebook includes quality of a single output within usefulness, so a separate novelty or overall-creativity dimension is not required for this output-quality outcome. This is a coding judgment applying the codebook to the stated rubric, not a claim that the paper measured originality or diversity. Update the corresponding explanation in eligibility.reason; retain core=no and context_class=none because only 36 people were analyzed. Random assignment to DALL-E 3 versus ArchDaily with this scored output warrants has_randomized_people_study=true and two-screener review.
corrections.quote: The rubric includes three core dimensions, clarity and legibility, complexity and detail, and overall visual communication.
corrections.locator: PDF p. 11 [printed 9], Section 3.5 and Table 1; random assignment: PDF pp. 6-7 [printed 4-5], Section 3.1, and p. 10 [printed 8], Section 3.4.2; creativity-codebook.md, Sections 1, 3, and 6 (usefulness includes quality of a single output).

confirmed: The source read is the 41-page local preprint retrieved from arxiv.org/pdf/2601.10696, not the journal article. Its title and four authors match the form; the PDF modification date is 2026-09-10 and no arXiv version identifier is printed. The entire markdown conversion, including References, was read (PDF pp. 1-41; PDF metadata; retrieval.json, c133.source_url).

One individual-randomized laboratory study compares DALL-E 3 within ChatGPT-4 with ArchDaily precedent search after a common initial design phase; lab_rct and ai_vs_active are correct (PDF pp. 6-11 [printed 4-9], Sections 3.1-3.5).

Section 3.1 first states 41 recruited and randomly assigned, followed by 5 noncompleters, then also describes the retained 36 as randomly assigned. The form correctly flags this ambiguity: 36 people were analyzed, 18 per arm, and initial per-arm allocation counts are not supplied (PDF pp. 6-7 [printed 4-5], Section 3.1).

Participants came from varied disciplines, not solely architecture; Control had 8 women and GenAI had 9. Core=no, criterion_2=not_met, and context_class=none are correct because 36 analyzed people is below 50 (PDF pp. 6-7 [printed 4-5], Section 3.1; codebook Section 3).

The 72 drawings are outputs from 36 participants across two phases. Eight judges, four professors and four senior students, scored three rubric dimensions on a 1-5 scale; composite ICCs were 0.157 and 0.208 (PDF p. 11 [printed 9], Section 3.5 and Table 1).

The initial and revision phases each lasted 30 minutes within an approximately 1.5-hour individual session, following a roughly one-hour tutorial. Revision instructions requested at least five concepts; the drawing tablet was 15.6 inches (PDF pp. 8-11 [printed 6-9], Sections 3.3-3.4.2).

The performance reported string is numerically exact: Revision phase: Control 2.785 ± 0.361 vs GenAI 2.903 ± 0.433, p = 0.381, Cohen's d = 0.296 (n = 18 per arm). Initial phase: Control 2.921 ± 0.369 vs GenAI 2.819 ± 0.388, p = 0.426, d = -0.269. DiD = 0.583 SDs, 95% CI [-0.476, 1.643]. (PDF p. 15 [printed 13], Table 3, and p. 16 [printed 14], Table 4 and Section 4.2).

The general creative self-efficacy reported string is numerically exact: Revision phase: Control 3.741 ± 0.805 vs GenAI 3.574 ± 0.899, p = 0.562, d = -0.195. DiD = -0.54 SDs, 95% CI [-1.068, -0.017] (text: DiD = -0.543). The table-versus-prose rounding difference is correctly retained (PDF p. 15 [printed 13], Table 3, and p. 16 [printed 14], Table 4 and Section 4.2).

The one-line finding accurately reports the nonsignificant design-performance contrast and the negative general creative self-efficacy DiD. General creative self-efficacy averages self-report items Q3-Q5 and is not an output-scored outcome (PDF p. 12 [printed 10], Section 3.6 and Table 2; PDF pp. 15-16 [printed 13-14], Tables 3-4).

DiD estimates and their 95% intervals use the pooled SD of initial-phase scores; standard errors are clustered by participant. The study was not formally preregistered (PDF p. 14 [printed 12], Section 3.8; PDF p. 16 [printed 14], Table 4 note).

Interaction analyses used 16 GenAI participants after 2 missing recordings and 17 Control participants after 1 missing recording; these are not the main design-rating sample sizes. The 3-26 prompt range refers to the 16 recorded GenAI users (PDF pp. 18-19 [printed 16-17], Sections 4.4-4.5).

Tables S1-S3 and Fig. S1 are cited but are absent from the supplied PDF, which ends with References. Their stated subjects match the form; no additional appendix was available in this document (PDF p. 7, Section 3.1; p. 12, Section 3.6; p. 16, Section 4.2; p. 18, Section 4.3; p. 41, end of References).

This is an original experiment, not a synthesis; leaving synthesis counts and pooled estimates empty is correct. Funding is attributed to the U.S. National Science Foundation, and no competing interests are declared (PDF pp. 6-14, Methodology; pp. 26-27 [printed 24-25], Acknowledgements and Declaration of competing interest).
summary: This randomized laboratory study analyzed 36 students and scored their design quality, a usefulness outcome under the codebook, so it warrants two-screener review but fails the 50-person threshold. All reported statistics match the PDF; corrections concern outcome eligibility, the initial-phase wood-block aid, and the omitted OSF data URL.
